MARTINEZ GROUP MEDICAL GROUP - DISCHARGE SUMMARY

Patient: Steven Velazquez DOB: 11/02/1945 Sex: M MRN: 905857

Admit: 01/12/2016 Discharge: 01/21/2016

Principal diagnosis: Coronary artery disease, s/p myocardial infarction (event at age 70; 9 yrs ago; event MI; EF 62%; 1-vessel disease; LDL 66)
Secondary diagnoses: BPH; eczema; vitamin D deficiency

Hospital Steven Velazquez, a 78-year-old male with a history of coronary artery disease (CAD) status post myocardial infarction (MI) at age 70, was admitted on January 12, 2016, for routine follow-up and management of his chronic conditions. He has been under the care of Dr. Stacey Walton, Family Medicine, at Martinez Group Medical Group.

Upon admission, Mr. Velazquez reported no new or worsening symptoms. He has been compliant with his medication regimen and has been managing his conditions well. His last visit was on September 18, 2024, where his blood pressure was 137/76 mmHg, and his weight was 241 pounds. His previous visits showed stable vitals and weights, with the highest recorded weight of 245 pounds on November 26, 2023, and the lowest of 230 pounds on April 10, 2022.

Mr. Velazquez's coronary artery disease is well-controlled with medications, including atorvastatin 20 mg, aspirin 81 mg, and metoprolol 50 mg. His ejection fraction (EF) is 62%, indicating good cardiac function. His LDL cholesterol level is 66 mg/dL, which is within the target range for his condition. He has no history of angina and has been adherent to his medication regimen.

His benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) is managed with finasteride 1 mg, and he reports no significant urinary symptoms. His eczema is controlled with triamcinolone topical 0.1%, and he has no active skin lesions. His vitamin D deficiency is managed with ergocalciferol 50000 IU, and his levels have been within the normal range on recent lab tests.

Mr. Velazquez has a family history significant for myocardial infarction in his father at age 49, who passed away at age 58. He is a former smoker, having quit cigarettes on February 5, 2022, after smoking 10 per day since November 27, 1967. He consumes approximately one alcoholic drink per week and engages in regular physical activity, running 3-4 times per week.

During his hospital stay, Mr. Velazquez underwent a series of routine tests and evaluations, including a physical examination, electrocardiogram (ECG), and laboratory tests. All results were within normal limits, and no acute issues were identified. He was educated on the importance of medication adherence, lifestyle modifications,

FAX 6  ##
and regular follow-up appointments.

Discharge medications:
- Atorvastatin 20 mg daily
- Aspirin 81 mg daily
- Metoprolol 50 mg daily
- Finasteride 1 mg daily
- Triamcinolone topical 0.1% as needed for eczema
- Ergocalciferol 50000 IU weekly

Discharge instructions:
Mr. Velazquez was discharged home in stable condition on January 21, 2016. He was instructed to continue his current medication regimen and maintain his regular exercise routine. He was advised to follow up with his primary care physician, Dr. Stacey Walton, for routine monitoring of his chronic conditions. He was also encouraged to maintain a healthy diet, avoid tobacco use, and limit alcohol consumption.

Follow-up:
Mr. Velazquez is scheduled for a follow-up appointment with Dr. Walton in one month to review his lab results and overall health status. He was provided contact information for the Martinez Group Medical Group should he experience any concerning symptoms or have questions about his care.

This discharge summary was prepared by Dr. Stacey Walton, Family Medicine, Martinez Group Medical Group.
